subject: On-prem cluster footprint, nodetypes and storage slicing — planning review
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-eng@timberhealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Timber Health on-prem kickoff — initial requirements + attachments

Team — attaching the first-pass requirements Timber Health sent yesterday. They want a private Redwood deployment in their colocation racks. High level asks: HIPAA adjacency, ability to pin model versions, predictable p99 latency < 200ms for small chat workloads, and an offline-friendly canary plan.

Requesting quick feedback on the following so we can shape the SOW:
- Cluster footprint (control plane HA vs single-zone control plane)
- Node classes (GPU inference, batch, infra) and minimum CPU/memory/gpu profiles
- Storage plan: NVMe local for KV cache? shared persistent volumes for model artifacts?
- Network topology: separate management VPC, customer firewall requirements, egress constraints

Attachments: redwood-onprem-reqs-v1.pdf (customer requirements), node-class-profiles.xlsx (starter profiles)

Thanks — can we take 30m tomorrow to align?

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-eng@timberhealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timber Health on-prem kickoff — initial requirements + attachments

Thanks Dev — skimmed the doc. Quick reactions inline and a few questions: 

- Control plane: Timber calls for regional HA but their rack footprint is two pods in a single colocation. My leaning: recommend control-plane HA across two AZ-equivalent racks with external etcd quorum (3 nodes) and kube-api in HA. If Timber insists single-rack, we should document the SLA delta.

- KV cache: would like to propose local NVMe on inference nodes for LLM KV cache to get deterministic latency. We'll need a fallback remote cache (Redis/Elasticache-like) for cold restarts. Do we have a recommended sizing rule of thumb (nvme per GPU) we can propose?

- PVs: customer asked for model artifacts on shared PVs to make rolling updates easier. Are we comfortable recommending Rook/Ceph backed PVs for model artifacts + Longhorn for smaller critical state? Concern: Ceph ops for Timber may be heavy.

Questions:
1) What taints/tolerations do we want to standardize for inference-gpu vs batch?
2) Any firm guidance on ephemeral scratch disk sizes per pod?
3) Network: do we require a dedicated out-of-band management NIC for node lifecycle (PXE/IMPI) or is their current remote-BMC setup sufficient?

Happy to run a 30m tomorrow 10:30am PT.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, infra-eng@timberhealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timber Health on-prem kickoff — initial requirements + attachments

On Wed, Sep 9, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Dev — skimmed the doc. Quick reactions inline and a few questions:

Good notes. I sketched a pragmatic, ops-friendly node-class + storage approach below that balances performance and operational burden for Timber Health:

Proposed node classes (minimal recommended counts):
- control-plane (3 x m5-like) — etcd + kube control plane, anti-affinity across racks
- infra-utility (2) — logging/metrics, ingress controllers, cert mgmt, and NATS/Kafka clients
- inference-gpu (N, 1 GPU each as baseline) — NVMe local for KV cache + 200Gi ephemeral scratch
- model-storage (2) — Rook/Ceph OSDs on HDD+SSD mix for object store of artifacts (models, snapshots)
- storage-fast (2) — NVMe-backed nodes presenting PVCs for high-iops DBs (if customer needs DBs co-located)
- batch-cpu (2) — autoscaling group for large background conversions

Storage recommendations:
- KV cache: local NVMe per inference node. Rule of thumb: 200Gi NVMe per V100-equivalent GPU for multi-turn short-window workloads; increase to 400Gi for long-context models.
- Model artifacts: object storage on Rook/Ceph because Timber wants shared mounts for canary swapping. Offer a managed Rook deployment with automated OSD placement and documented recovery steps.
- Critical small-state PVs: Longhorn deployed on infra-utility nodes for easier snapshots and quicker recovery.

Network and security:
- Management plane: require a separate management VLAN; BMC or console access must be on this VLAN and firewalled from compute.
- Egress: all outbound traffic from model nodes must go through a controlled NAT/gateway with TLS inspection exceptions; we will provide a list of allowed domains for model telemetry.
- KMS: integrate with customer KMS (Vault/HSM) for disk encryption keys. Document key rotation cadence.

Taints/tolerations:
- inference-gpu: taint key=inference:NoSchedule, tolerations for runtime and model puller init containers
- storage-fast: taint=storage:PreferNoSchedule for production scheduling control

Canary plan (high level):
- Create a separate canary model namespace with scaled-down inference-gpu nodes (1-2 nodes) and identical NVMe config
- Traffic split via service mesh ingress (10% canary -> 90% prod initially) with metrics gating (latency, error rate, token drift)

I'll convert this into a short one-pager and attach node-class-profiles.xlsx with concrete sizes. Happy to adjust numbers based on Timber's rack specs.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha King <samantha.king@timberhealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Timber Health on-prem kickoff — initial requirements + attachments

Thanks everyone — the proposal looks sensible and in line with our compliance team expectations. A few clarifications before we schedule the onsite design session: 

- Encryption: we require AES-256 at rest with KMS integration. We operate AWS KMS and have an HSM-backed rotation policy. Can Redwood support external KMS for disk keys?
- Ceph ops: our SREs prefer a lighter operational model. If Rook/Ceph is operationally heavy, would Redwood support an object-store-only design (S3-compatible gateway) backed by local object nodes, or alternatively provide a managed Rook operating runbook?
- Canary: we need a documented rollback window and a way to automatically fail traffic to a safe model variant if token drift exceeds threshold. Can you include a recommended telemetry gating plan?

Also attaching a short compliance checklist the team's SOC engineer put together — please confirm items we need to document for procurement.

— Samantha King
Sr. Infrastructure Lead, Timber Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@timberhealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timber Health on-prem kickoff — initial requirements + attachments

Samantha — thanks, great questions. Short answers and next steps: 

- KMS: yes — we can integrate with Timber's AWS KMS for disk encryption keys using a customer-managed key policy. We'll include a key-rotation appendix in the SOW. (Action: Dev to draft KMS integration steps)
- Ceph: understood. Two options for the SOW:
  1) Managed Rook deployment with runbook + on-call support window (recommended if Timber wants shared POSIX mounts and frequent artifact updates)
  2) S3-compatible object gateway (lighter ops) with model-server side logic to stage models locally for canaries (lower operational overhead but more complexity in model rollout flows)

- Canary gating: propose a telemetry set: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-request error rate, token-diff score against a small verification prompt set, and a model-quality regression alert. If any gating metric exceeds the threshold for 5 consecutive minutes, we auto-rollback traffic to the prior stable variant and page ops. (Action: Marissa to draft the canary gating matrix and attach canary-rollout-matrix.md)

Action items: 
- Dev: draft KMS appendix + walkbook for key integration (due Tue 9/14)
- Marissa: canary gating matrix doc and initial telemetry thresholds (due Mon 9/13)
- Laura: convert node-class list to final sizing based on Timber rack spec (need rack spec by 9/15)
- Jordan: schedule on-site design session for week of 9/20 (I'll send invites after we confirm rack spec)

Filing the shared assets here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3c-example-onprem-plan and JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-8241 created to track deliverables.

— Jordan
Director, Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
